In cross-section, the shaft of the penis is built around three cylindrical columns of vascular sinusoidal tissue wrapped in tough collagenous sleeves. Known in classical anatomical nomenclature as Corpora cavernosa · corpus spongiosum, this chapter belongs to the male reproductive study pathway. The paired corpora cavernosa are enveloped by strong tunica albuginea and form the main rigid erectile compartment; the ventral corpus spongiosum surrounds the penile urethra and expands distally as the glans. Deep penile arteries feed cavernous spaces. Parasympathetic-associated cavernous neural signaling relaxes smooth muscle, increasing arterial inflow and restricting subtunical venous outflow. The spongiosum remains comparatively compliant to protect urethral patency.

When you trace how penile erectile tissue anatomy functions in the living body, each documented landmark contributes a specific mechanical or physiological step. Key structures covered in this guide include Paired corpora cavernosa (primary rigid erectile compartment), Corpus spongiosum (engorges without compressing urethral lumen closed), Tunica albuginea (resists expansion and aids venous occlusion), and Cavernosal trabeculae (relaxation permits filling of cavernous lacunae). By following all 20 illustrated landmarks in sequence, you can see how gross morphology, internal chambers or layers, and surrounding vessels work as one integrated unit.

Understanding these structural relationships is essential for both anatomy exams and real-world physiological reasoning. Practical anatomical correlations also stand out: for paired corpora cavernosa, fibrous tunica helps compress emissary venous outflow; for corpus spongiosum, its distal expansion is the glans penis. questions.question: What are the three erectile bodies of the penis?
questions.answer: Two paired corpora cavernosa form the main dorsal erectile cylinders. A single corpus spongiosum surrounds the urethra and expands into the glans. From an anatomical and functional standpoint, its distal expansion is the glans penis.

questions.question: What does the tunica albuginea do in erectile tissue?
questions.answer: It is a dense connective-tissue covering around erectile compartments, particularly strong around the corpora cavernosa. In relation to paired corpora cavernosa, this structure primary rigid erectile compartment. From an anatomical and functional standpoint, fibrous tunica helps compress emissary venous outflow.

questions.question: What are the paired corpora cavernosa?
questions.answer: Two dorsal longitudinal erectile cylinders that unite in shaft and separate proximally as crura. Function: Primary rigid erectile compartment. In relation to paired corpora cavernosa, this structure primary rigid erectile compartment.

questions.question: Where is the tunica albuginea located?
questions.answer: Strong fibrous sheath encasing cavernosa, with distinct collagen layers. Function: Resists expansion and aids venous occlusion. In relation to tunica albuginea, this structure resists expansion and aids venous occlusion. From an anatomical and functional standpoint, disruption during trauma can constitute penile fracture.

questions.question: What is the function of the deep penile arteries?
questions.answer: Function: Feed cavernosal tissue. Internal pudendal branches traveling within each corpus cavernosum. In relation to deep penile arteries, this structure feed cavernosal tissue. Functionally, deep penile arteries feed cavernosal tissue.
